_note: The tagging matrix (docs/plan-verification-and-tickets.md, Phase 1; agreed 2026-09-18). The scan can read what code DOES; it cannot read what code is FOR. These tags supply the intent, declared IN the code (headers, feature READMEs) so anyone with a clone can read the architecture with no tool. Cockpit is one reader: the scanner verifies each declaration against what the code does, and every finding is the gap between the two. Only declared things are here; what Cockpit computes (reads/writes, reach, impact, churn, coverage, sensitivity by inference, the findings, which tickets touched a file) is never declared - a claim about those would be the lie the doctrine warns about. Precedence: hand-set in Cockpit (the owner's) > declared in the code > inferred by the scan. A tag enters through this file (a ticket); its appliesTo says whose job it is to carry it, so the next scan lists every file that should carry it and does not (tag-missing), and a tag not in this file is tag-unknown - nothing enters through a single file. The doc generator (ARCHITECTURE.md, the README template) and the scanner read this one source.

header.syntax: one tag per line, or all on one line, in the language's comment form: // @feature tasks   -- @feature tasks (SQL)   <!-- @feature tasks @kind screen --> (HTML)

contract: ## Tables - one owned table per line
## Flows - one per line: `- name: step → step → step` (a step is a screen or an action by name)
## Seed - optional: what the flows need in the test database
readme.why: a feature exists when its README exists: the README is the vocabulary entry, readable with no tool

kinds.rule: every arrow goes ONE column to the right: screen → action → logic → data. A screen never touches a table, a door (action) never queries, data never reaches back, one feature never writes another's table.
kinds.why: the four kinds are the shape every feature keeps; tests, scripts and tooling are outside the shape and carry @kind test or @kind tool

feature.usedFor: grouping - what is this file part of; what features exist and what belongs to each; what am I touching with this ticket; which feature is riskiest, least tested, most changed
feature.values: any name; a feature exists when its README exists; `shared` for code every feature uses; one feature per file

kind.usedFor: the shape - which of the four is this; is the code shaped as the architecture says; where does an arrow skip a column or run backwards

flow.usedFor: paths and testing - which user paths does this file take part in; which test proves each path; if I change this file, which paths must be re-tested; which paths have no test; what does a person actually do that this code serves
where: file header of screens and tests (actions inherit from the screens that call them, and may declare too)
flow.values: the README's list; comma-separated when a file takes part in several

purpose.required: new files; tag-missing on old ones until rolled out
purpose.usedFor: understanding - what is this file for, in one sentence, so anyone opening it knows before reading the code

tables.usedFor: ownership - who owns this table; who else writes it, and should not; which feature's data does this change reach
tables.values: the table names the feature owns, one per line

auth.usedFor: intended access - what is this door supposed to require, so the scan can compare with what it does
auth.changesBy: the schema (to require it), then ticket

sensitive.usedFor: intended exposure - what a table holds when its name and columns do not say; overrides inference

computedNotDeclared.why: a claim about these would be the lie the doctrine warns about; the scan reads them from the code and they ARE the verification
list: which tickets touched a file (git log - every commit and PR names its ticket)

findings._note: the verify ids above; each becomes a rule in problems.json under a Declarations block when the reader lands (Phase 2)
findings.tag-without-readme: a file names a feature that has no README
findings.readme-without-files: a feature README with no file carrying its @feature
findings.file-untagged: a file with no @feature (the migration backlog on an old codebase)
findings.kind-disagrees: the declared kind disagrees with what the file does - a logic file declaring routes, a screen reading a table
findings.kind-unknown: a @kind value not in this schema
findings.flow-without-test: a flow in a README that no test names
findings.test-names-unknown-flow: a test naming a flow no README defines
findings.flow-not-in-feature: a screen naming a flow its feature does not define
findings.flow-step-missing: a flow step naming a screen or action that does not exist
findings.purpose-missing: a file with no @purpose (new files: required; old files: the rollout backlog)
findings.owned-table-written-elsewhere: a README's owned table written from another feature
findings.listed-table-undefined: a README lists a table nothing defines
findings.auth-disagrees: the declared requirement disagrees with the check the code makes
findings.tag-missing: a file that should carry a tag (by appliesTo) and does not - the rollout list when a tag is added
findings.tag-unknown: a @tag not in this schema - nothing enters through a single file
